The printed footer shows 'V-2025-06' (Hubbard's month/year print-code) and a copyright line '© 2025 Hubbard'. No single explicit 'published on' sentence appears in the body text.
notes: CANDIDATE FILE - NOT YET IMPORTED. Transcribed from the 'PARENT STOCK FEMALE FEEDING AND BODYWEIGHT OBJECTIVES - REARING PERIOD' table (Dark house / Open house in season column only; the 'Difficult conditions / Open side house out of season' variant column is intentionally omitted, mirroring how the existing Ross 308 profile omits its out-of-season variant), the 'PARENT STOCK FEMALE FEEDING AND BODYWEIGHT STANDARD - PRODUCTION PERIOD' table (before-feeding bodyweight only for weeks 25-64), and the 'PARENT STOCK FEMALE PRODUCTION OBJECTIVES' table (weeks 25-64 / production weeks 1-40). Values are exactly as published; no interpolation or estimation. This document is a condensed 8-page leaflet: it contains NO male body weight/feeding table, NO liveability/mortality data, NO cumulative hatchability column, NO egg mass column, and NO performance-summary page - these are absent from the source, not omitted by choice, and are recorded as gaps in the validation block below rather than filled with derived numbers.

body_weight_g.table: Parent Stock Female Feeding and Bodyweight Objectives - Rearing Period (weeks 1-24, Dark house / Open house in season column) / Parent Stock Female Feeding and Bodyweight Standard - Production Period (weeks 25-64)
body_weight_g.footnote: Rearing table footnote: 'Birds are weighed before feeding.' The Production Period table publishes bodyweight from week 25 onward as a 'Bodyweight before feeding / Bodyweight after feeding' pair (e.g. week 25: '3088 / 3211'); only the before-feeding value is captured here for consistency with the rearing table's weighing convention. The after-feeding value is NOT captured in this profile.
body_weight_g.note: Weeks 20-24 appear in both source tables with identical published values (cross-checked: 2250/2430/2602/2768/2930 g in both), confirming internal consistency of the two tables.

daily_feed_intake_g.table: Parent Stock Female Feeding and Bodyweight Objectives - Rearing Period (Dark house / Open house in season column)
daily_feed_intake_g.note: Weeks 1-2 publish only 'Ad lib (24)' / 'Ad lib (30)' (a bracketed reference number alongside 'Ad lib' text, not a feed weight) and are omitted rather than guessed. No feed ration is published for weeks 25-64 in either table available in this document (the Production Period table leaves the Ration/ME columns blank from week 25 onward and refers the reader to a separate production-percentage-indexed feeding table, 'Female feeding in production', which cannot be mapped onto an age-day/age-week axis without inventing an age-to-production-% correspondence) - so this metric's series stops at week 24 (ageDays 168).

eggs_per_hen_housed_weekly.note: The published heading is literally 'Total eggs' (not 'Eggs/Bird/Week Hen-Housed' as in the Ross 308 profile). Reused this metric code because the magnitude and behaviour (weekly count per hen, summing to the published cumulative column) match the same concept; the heading is recorded here verbatim rather than renamed in the schema.

egg_weight_g.note: An adjacent 'Egg weight (lb/doz)' imperial column is also published but not captured (out of scope for this metric, which is defined in grams). Source row for production week 30 (age week 54) prints an anomalous lb/doz value ('1.25') inconsistent with the surrounding trend (~1.79-1.81); this does not affect the captured gram value (68.1) but is flagged in validation/uncertainties as a probable print artifact in the PDF.

hatching_egg_utilization_weekly_pct.note: Only one utilization percentage column is published per row (not split into weekly/cumulative variants as in the Ross profile); it is captured as the weekly value because it is derivable from the same row's weekly Total-eggs and weekly Hatching-eggs figures. No cumulative hatching-egg-utilization percentage is published, so hatching_egg_utilization_cumulative_pct is not populated for this profile.

hatchability_all_eggs_weekly_pct.footnote: **** Hatchability: based on eggs stored for less than 7 days
hatchability_all_eggs_weekly_pct.note: Only a single weekly hatchability percentage column is published; there is no cumulative hatchability column in this document, so hatchability_cumulative_pct is not populated for this profile.

gapsFromSourceDocument: Male body weight and feeding program - not published in this document at all (no male table of any kind appears in the 8-page EDGE leaflet).
Liveability / mortality (rearing and laying period) - not published.

Egg mass (g) - not published as a distinct column (only egg weight is given; egg mass would require multiplying by hen-week % as Ross does, which was not done here to avoid computing a value the source does not itself publish).
Cumulative hatchability (%) - only a weekly hatchability figure is published.
Cumulative hatching-egg utilization (%) - only a weekly utilization figure is published.

Performance summary page (peak %, total flock totals, depletion age stated explicitly, liveability) - the document has no such summary page; all headline figures reported below were read directly off the weekly tables rather than a published summary.

Female daily feeding at onset of production (production-percentage indexed feeding table) - present in the PDF but indexed by production percentage milestones (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 60%, >70%) rather than by age, so it cannot be placed on the ageDays/ageWeek axis this schema uses without inventing an age correspondence; skipped entirely rather than guessed.

validation.ageDaysAgeWeekConsistency: PASS - all 526 value rows satisfy ageDays == ageWeek * 7.

contiguousWeekSequences.body_weight_g: PASS - weeks 1-64 contiguous, no gaps (64 rows; week 0 has no published bodyweight value, only 'Ad lib' feeding text, so the series begins at week 1 as in the source).
contiguousWeekSequences.daily_feed_intake_g: PARTIAL - weeks 3-24 contiguous (22 rows). Weeks 1-2 omitted because the source publishes only 'Ad lib' text for those weeks, not a numeric ration. Series does not continue past week 24 because no feed data is published for weeks 25-64 in an age-indexed table (see gapsFromSourceDocument).
contiguousWeekSequences.egg/production-cycle metrics (hen_week_p: PASS - all contiguous, production weeks 1-40 / age weeks 25-64, no gaps, 40 rows each.

validation.unitAgreement: PASS - body_weight_g in grams throughout (the parallel lb column was not captured, matching the Ross profile's precedent of capturing only the metric column); daily_feed_intake_g in g/bird/day (cross-checked against the parallel lb/100-females column at several rows, e.g. week 3: 32 g vs 7.0 lb/100 females -> 7.0*453.6/100=31.75g, consistent within rounding); all percentage metrics in %; egg_weight_g in grams (lb/doz column not captured).

cumulativeCountSeriesNonDecreasing.eggs_per_hen_housed_cumulative: PASS - strictly non-decreasing across all 40 weeks (0.4 -> 181.8).
cumulativeCountSeriesNonDecreasing.hatching_eggs_per_hen_housed_cumulative: PASS - strictly non-decreasing across all 40 weeks (0.2 -> 174.7).
cumulativeCountSeriesNonDecreasing.chicks_per_hen_housed_cumulative: PASS - strictly non-decreasing across all 40 weeks (0.1 -> 149.6).

validation.cumulativePercentageSeriesNote: hen_week_production_pct and hen_housed_production_pct are per-week instantaneous percentages, not cumulative percentages, and rise then fall over the cycle as expected (peaking around production weeks 6-7); this decline in later weeks is the expected biological pattern and is not flagged as an error.
spotChecks: Page 2 (rearing table), week 24 / age 168 days: bodyweight 2930 g, ration 134 g/day, ME 369 kcal - matches text extraction exactly.
Page 3 (production period table), week 25 / age 175 days: bodyweight before/after feeding '3088 / 3211' g - before-feeding value 3088 captured as body_weight_g; matches.
Page 3 (production period table), week 64 / age 448 days: bodyweight before/after feeding '4147 / 4312' g - before-feeding value 4147 captured as the final body_weight_g row; matches.
Page 4 (production objectives table), production week 7 (age week 31): % prod./HW = 87.1, the highest hen-week percentage value in the whole table - confirmed as the published peak.

Page 4 (production objectives table), production week 6 (age week 30): % prod./HH = 86.0, the highest hen-housed percentage value in the whole table - confirmed as the published peak (one week earlier than the HW peak, which is internally consistent since HH already reflects cumulative mortality drag).

Page 4 (production objectives table), final row (age week 64 / production week 40): Total eggs cum. = 181.8, Hatching eggs cum. = 174.7, Chicks cum. = 149.6 - matches text extraction exactly and is used as the headline end-of-cycle figures below.

Page 4 footnotes verbatim: '* HW: Hen per Week', '** HH: Hen Housed', '*** Hatching egg: minimum 50 g', '**** Hatchability: based on eggs stored for less than 7 days' - all four captured into metricProvenance.
validation.knownSourceAnomaly: Production objectives table, age week 54 (production week 30) row: the Egg weight (lb/doz) column prints '1.25', which breaks the smooth upward trend of surrounding rows (~1.79-1.81 lb/doz for adjacent weeks). This looks like a print/typesetting defect in the source PDF. It does not affect this profile because the lb/doz column was not captured (only the gram value, 68.1 g, which fits the trend normally); flagged here for transparency in case a future profile ever needs the imperial column.
